claims.claim: Bounded exhaustive search for a shortest distinguishing trace over a finite input alphabet is a solved problem and nothing about the search in this package is a contribution.
claims.evidence: PRIOR_ART_MATRIX.md: trace equivalence, bisimulation, refinement, CEGAR, differential testing; ParDiff (OOPSLA 2024) performs static differential analysis across multiple protocol-parser implementations for exactly this purpose.

claims.claim: Separating a measurement value from a status coordinate, and specifying how the status must propagate, is standardised prior art.
claims.evidence: ARINC 429 SSM; SEVA (Henry & Clarke 1993); NAMUR NE 107; OPC UA StatusCode. OPC UA Part 8 / OPC 30142 additionally specify the merge rule (worst-of severity across an array), which is an allowed-merge clause in a published conformance specification.

claims.claim: The state model in CANONICAL_STATE_MODEL.md -- specifically that merging two distinct kinds of absence loses information the consumer needs -- is prior art.
claims.evidence: Codd's A-marks and I-marks (missing-but-applicable vs inapplicable), 1979; SQL's conflation of them and its consequences have been studied for forty years.

claims.claim: That coarsening an observation can destroy diagnosability is prior art, in exactly this form.
claims.evidence: DES diagnosability under observation masks (Sampath et al. 1995 and successors); abstraction-based failure diagnosis (Schmidt 2009) gives conditions under which abstraction preserves diagnosability.

claims.claim: That local per-stage preservation guarantees compose to an end-to-end guarantee is a trivial induction, and the general compositional theory is complete.
claims.evidence: COMPOSITIONAL_ANALYSIS.md; assume-guarantee contracts (Benveniste et al.; Pacti, ACM TCPS 2025).

claims.claim: This repository ALREADY contains a per-channel machine-readable semantic contract that states the required distinctions in prose, and nothing checks that the pipeline honours them.
claims.evidence: docs/simulation/CHANNEL_SEMANTICS.yaml carries missing_semantics per channel: gnss.position 'fix_type < 3 is NOT a zero position. It is MISSING with reason NO_3D_FIX.'; battery.current '-1 means "not measured" -> MISSING, not zero current'; mag.field_ut 'all-zero triple is treated as ABSENT, not as a zero field'. The field is loaded at qualification.py:83 and used at exactly one site, qualification.py:243, as a note= string on a NOT_RECEIVED ChannelValue. tests/test_channel_semantics.py:28 checks only that it is non-empty.
claims.note: This is the closest prior art of all and it is internal. It means the CONTENT of ARDUPILOT_INGEST_CONTRACTS/*.json is largely a restatement of existing documentation.

claims.claim: On the v1.1 ArduPilot adapter, an explicit no-3D-fix report and no message at all are indistinguishable at every pipeline stage from the core bridge onward, and the first stage that destroys the distinction is to_core_samples (csia/aircraft/adapters/base.py:306-337), NOT the adapter's GNSS branch.
claims.evidence: CAUSAL_BLAME_TRACES.json, family gnss, clause GNSS-F1: T1-T4 differ, T5-T9 identical. Shortest witness 'I', length 1, exhaustive over 120 words of length <= 4.
claims.note: Item 22's illustrative example attributes this collapse to the adapter. Measured, that attribution is wrong for this codebase: the adapter pops the retained fix and records MissingReason.NO_3D_FIX, and both survive to T4.

claims.claim: The bridge into the frozen core has a two-token output alphabet (emit with valid=True, or emit nothing) while the adapter upstream can express up to six states, so no three-state source distinction can survive it.
claims.evidence: base.py:335 writes chans['valid'] = True unconditionally; the only alternative is base.py:312-318's `break`. Measured emitted vocabularies: gnss v1_1_adapter ['V'], plugins_py ['I','V'], ulog_source_py ['I','V'].
claims.note: This is the data-processing inequality with the constant made explicit. The inequality is known (item 20 says so); only the identification of the specific line is new information, and it is information about this codebase.

claims.claim: Three committed decoders give one raw condition (BATTERY_STATUS.current_battery == -1) three different currents into the same frozen core: 5.00 A, 0.00 A and -1.00 A.
claims.evidence: Measured at T5 on word 'X': v1_1_adapter emits (V, 5.0) -- the previous reading retained because ardupilot.py:181 does not pop _latest; plugins_py emits (M, 0.0) from max(msg.current_battery, 0)/100.0 at plugins.py:194; ulog_source_py emits (V, -1.0) because ulog_source.py:196-199 sets valid=True unconditionally. None can emit X; the contract requires ['V','X'].

claims.claim: The ulog_source.py battery finding is not synthetic: the committed 9.6 MB PX4 log carries current_a == -1.0 on all 216 battery_status samples.
claims.evidence: results/PX4_FEASIBILITY.json, real_log.battery: 216 samples, min -1.0, max -1.0, negative_samples 216. On this real log ulog_source.py would feed -1.00 A into the frozen core as a usable battery current 216 times.

claims.claim: The magnetometer collapses TWO STAGES EARLIER than GNSS or battery on the same path, at T3_ingest, because ardupilot.py:143 has no else branch at all -- no _put and no _reject_sentinel, so the adapter's state after an all-zero triple is identical to its state after no message.
claims.evidence: CAUSAL_BLAME_TRACES.json, family mag, clause MAG-F1, path v1_1_adapter: first_collapse_stage T3_ingest. Shortest collapsing pair 'Z'/'N', length 1.
claims.note: This is the evidence that the stage localisation does work rather than always naming the same boundary: three families on one path give first collapses at T3, T5 and T5.

claims.claim: Divergence at one equivalence level does not propagate to the next, and this is measured rather than argued.
claims.evidence: EQUIVALENCE_LEVELS.md. Battery word 'X', v1_1_adapter vs ulog_source_py, all five controls clean: VALUE differs (5.00 A vs -1.00 A) while STATE, EVIDENCE, DIAGNOSIS and ASSURANCE are all identical. Battery, adapter vs plugins: 90/120 words diverge at STATE, only 15/120 at EVIDENCE.

claims.claim: The strongest downstream consequence measured anywhere in this package is a FAILSAFE LATENCY, not a different failsafe decision.
claims.evidence: 106 attributable ASSURANCE_STATE rows in DOWNSTREAM_CONSEQUENCES.csv, all gnss. In every one: identical level history NORMAL -> CAUTION, identical action set (SWITCH_NAV_INERTIAL, INHIBIT_GPS_MODES), escalation later by 0.32 s (80 rows) or 0.12 s (26 rows) on the v1.1 adapter. The action sets NEVER differ, on any word, in any family.
claims.note: CONTROL_FAILSAFE is not reached and is not claimed. Item 19: do not inflate severity when the consequence stops upstream.

claims.claim: No battery or magnetometer word produces any failsafe difference at all.
claims.evidence: ASSURANCE attributable divergences 0/120 for every battery pair and every mag pair. power_fault requires T['battery'] < 0.70, which battery trust does not reach in a 15 s run.
claims.note: The mechanism by which a CRITICAL could be raised on a disowned current is documented in ../dual_admissibility_confirmatory/BATTERY_DEFECT.md but was NOT observed here.

claims.claim: The path with careful MissingReason handling is the one that loses the GNSS distinction; the two paths that fabricate or forward a value keep it.
claims.evidence: GNSS-F1: v1_1_adapter FAIL, plugins_py PASS, ulog_source_py PASS.
claims.note: They keep it by accident -- neither has any notion of a reason -- but the distinction reaches the failsafe on both.

claims.claim: The GNSS collapse is a property of the shared core bridge, not of either autopilot: px4.py:220-227 is the same handling as ardupilot.py:226-236 and produces the same collapse at the same stage.
claims.evidence: results/PX4_FEASIBILITY.json: gnss agreement emitted_vocabulary_identical true, clause_results_identical true, first_collapse_identical true.

claims.claim: The PX4 platform is already protected from the battery defect, by a static per-channel declaration rather than by a preservation check.
claims.evidence: CHANNEL_SEMANTICS.yaml platform_qualification.px4 sets battery.current to UNAVAILABLE with a measured justification; the checker measures the PX4 emitted vocabulary for battery as [] -- nothing crosses into the core.

claims.claim: The checker detects all four deliberately injected instrument defects, and one of the four predictions about WHICH published quantity would move was wrong.
claims.evidence: TOOL_SELF_AUDIT.json: all_four_detected true, instrument_restored_exactly true, predictions_held 3/4, refuted D1_one_message_phase_shift.
claims.note: The refutation is kept and not re-aimed. It is informative: the A-close delay does not move under a one-message phase shift BECAUSE the no-fix report has no effect on admissibility on that path -- an independent confirmation of C7 arriving from an unexpected direction.

claims.claim: A domain-specific compositional corollary -- that end-to-end preservation is bounded by the narrowest inter-stage interface, so per-stage contracts are insufficient -- is a restatement of a bottleneck argument.
claims.evidence: COMPOSITIONAL_ANALYSIS.md. Worth writing in an engineering guideline; not a theorem and not new.

claims.claim: An automated end-to-end evidence-semantic checker for autonomy ingest paths is a novel research contribution.
claims.evidence: All four of item 26's kill conditions are met by existing work, individually: evidence semantics by NE 107 / SEVA / OPC UA / Codd; end-to-end status preservation by AUTOSAR E2E and by quality-flag propagation in data-reduction pipelines; minimal counterexamples by differential testing and ParDiff; diagnostic consequence by DES diagnosability under masks. What does not exist in one place is the combination, and a combination of four established techniques applied to one codebase is not a dissertation contribution.

claims.claim: Runtime verification of autonomy middleware against a formal interface specification is an open area where a sensor-quality-specific monitor would be new.
claims.evidence: RV for robotic middleware is active and published (RTLola ROS adapter RV 2025; RV4JaCa 2023; contract-based RV for modular robotic systems 2022). The shape of the checker here is the shape of those monitors.

claims.claim: E = ESTIMATED is a source-justified provenance state in this codebase.
claims.evidence: plugins.py:177 feeds GLOBAL_POSITION_INT -- EKF-fused output -- into the same `gps` core slot that otherwise carries raw receiver output, with no marker. The file's own comment (plugins.py:152-154) says why that matters.
claims.note: NOT EXERCISED by any word in this package: every alphabet carries GPS_RAW_INT. It is in the model as a state and not as a measurement.

claims.claim: The prior-art search in this package is complete enough to settle the novelty question.
claims.evidence: PRIOR_ART_MATRIX.md 'Method, and its limit': full-text retrieval was blocked by this environment's egress policy for every scholarly host attempted, so every row rests on title, venue and returned snippet.
claims.note: The limitation can only cause prior art to be UNDER-stated, so it does not threaten the KNOWN/SUBSUMED verdicts. It does mean the surviving-difference column may be too generous. IEC 61508 diagnostic coverage, AFDX/MIL-STD-1553 status words, active diagnosis, and the DDS SampleInfo.valid_data semantics remain unsearched.

claims.claim: The checker would find a defect needing a witness longer than 4 symbols.
claims.evidence: No such defect was looked for. The search is exhaustive to length 4 only; length 6 would cost roughly 30 minutes at the current per-word cost.
claims.note: Every counterexample found here has length <= 3, so the bound was never binding. That is not evidence that no longer witness exists.

refuted_predictions.prediction: A one-message phase shift would move the measured GNSS A-close delay.
refuted_predictions.outcome: REFUTED. It does not move, because the no-fix report does not affect admissibility on that path.

refuted_predictions.prediction: Item 22's example: the adapter is the first collapse for GNSS I vs N.
refuted_predictions.outcome: REFUTED. The adapter preserves the distinction through T3 and T4; the collapse is at T5, the core bridge.

refuted_predictions.prediction: The magnetometer would behave like GNSS and battery.
refuted_predictions.outcome: REFUTED. It collapses two stages earlier, at T3_ingest, because it has no rejection branch at all.

corrections_to_earlier_work.what: The first magnetometer runs were driven at 5 Hz against a 0.1 s core watchdog (STALE_TIMEOUT_S['mag']), so admissibility was closed between every message and no downstream consequence of the word could be observed.
corrections_to_earlier_work.fix: Per-family message rates (probe.py FAMILY_HZ); mag now runs at 20 Hz. The reason is recorded in the source so it is not repeated.
corrections_to_earlier_work.affected: all mag rows; re-run after the fix

corrections_to_earlier_work.what: The first version of proj_value returned the quality token rather than the numeric payload, so the VALUE and STATE levels were the same measurement under two names.
corrections_to_earlier_work.fix: T5_value is now recorded per path and proj_value compares numbers. This is what made the C12 counterexample visible.

corrections_to_earlier_work.what: The first version of first_collapse compared stage traces without times, so a stage that said the same things 0.5 s later looked identical.
corrections_to_earlier_work.fix: _collapse_timed keeps the first-appearance time of each token. This flipped GNSS-F1 from FAIL to PASS on plugins_py and ulog_source_py.

corrections_to_earlier_work.what: The first version named a collapse site in files that paths B and C never execute (they have no T3/T4).
corrections_to_earlier_work.fix: Stages absent from a path are skipped as collapse sites and reported as no_representation_stage.
